words.highlights.heading: Day 1's highs and lows
words.highlights.intro: Ten moments from Day 1 in the order they happened, four highs and six lows (I didn't even out the score). The lowest, at 13:20, runs five minutes uncut, because 24 minutes later the fix was a skill.
words.highlights.legend.hint: The numbers match: a triangle on any chart is the clip with the same number below.
words.highlights.comfy.label: Day 1, the highlight reel
words.highlights.scroll.hint: On a phone, the chart scrolls sideways.
words.highlights.map.title: Every named session, across the day
words.highlights.map.summary: {lanes} named Claude Code sessions ran on Day 1, starting {subagents} subagents between them. The one coordinating the rest started 174 by itself.
words.highlights.map.caption: One row per named session, a bar for each stretch it ran, 10:00 to midnight.
words.highlights.commits.title: Commits per hour
words.highlights.commits.summary: {commits} commits on Day 1. The busiest hour, {peak_hour}, had {peak}.
words.highlights.commits.caption: Single digits every hour until 13:00. The hour I closed every session still did 59 commits, and the hour after did 130.
words.highlights.subagents.title: Subagents started per hour
words.highlights.subagents.summary: {subagents} subagents started on Day 1. The busiest hour, {peak_hour}, had {peak}.
words.highlights.subagents.caption: A subagent is a helper a session starts for one job. Four an hour at most before 14:00, never fewer than 16 after.
words.highlights.folders.title: Where the commits landed
words.highlights.folders.summary: {commits} commits on Day 1 by folder. The most, {top}, went to {top_folder}.
words.highlights.folders.caption: Coordinating the sessions took one more commit than building the website, 134 to 133. Honestly, that's the job.
words.highlights.recording.title: Minutes on tape, per recording
words.highlights.recording.summary: {sessions} recordings, {hours} hours in all. The longest, {longest}, ran {longest_min} minutes.
words.highlights.recording.caption: {hours} hours on tape out of a 12-hour day. Some gaps are on purpose: the API keys got set up off camera.
words.highlights.beat.S02-f.label: Saying the thesis out loud
words.highlights.beat.S02-f.setup: Recording my intro, I said what this whole site argues: if AI won't cost you half your team, it goes in your pipeline first.
words.highlights.beat.S03-n.label: Noon, and nothing running yet
words.highlights.beat.S03-n.setup: The recording setup ate two hours of my morning, and at noon nothing ran in parallel: just me, on the bottleneck.
words.highlights.beat.S04-k.label: Bad feeling, no time to restart
words.highlights.beat.S04-k.setup: My own rule says a bad start is almost always worth starting over, and I had that feeling about the one document every session builds from.
words.highlights.beat.day1-2.label: Too many new things at once
words.highlights.beat.day1-2.setup: I made the day stressful on purpose so I'd focus, then stacked on too many firsts: recording all of it, building the site live, none of my usual setup.
words.highlights.beat.S07-d.label: The fix becomes a skill
words.highlights.beat.S07-d.setup: Whatever brought the sessions back after 13:20, I wanted it saved as a skill for the next accidental delete, power cut or crash.
words.highlights.beat.S08-c.label: What runs without me
words.highlights.beat.S08-c.setup: After lunch I walked through what runs without me, and why the site had been filling up on its own for an hour.
words.highlights.beat.S10-h.label: Halting everything to reset
words.highlights.beat.S10-h.setup: Too much was paused waiting on me, so I called it: anything not working on something specific halts, then it all restarts together.
words.highlights.beat.day1-5.label: The bottleneck was me
words.highlights.beat.day1-5.setup: At five o'clock I said it plainly: I shouldn't have started anything before two, and should have spent that time writing down exactly what I wanted.
words.highlights.beat.S12-a.label: Feeling 75% plus done
words.highlights.beat.S12-a.setup: Seven hours in, I was down to one agent, what was left was mostly design, and the part of my brain that does AI was pretty done.
words.highlights.centre.kill.title: One command, every session gone
words.highlights.centre.kill.setup: By 13:20 I had Claude Code sessions in the background, all working in parallel on this site, plus the ones that handle the recording. Lost in the weeds, I went to close the one I didn't need, and the command closed every one of them.
words.highlights.centre.kill.caption: Five minutes twenty, uncut. The one swear stays in.
words.highlights.centre.kill.seg.recovery: Handing the recovery to a fresh session
words.highlights.centre.kill.after: At 13:44 the whole recovery became a skill, so if it ever happens again, it's an instant fix.
